To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) The agents should learn concepts from each other in such a way that they are able to understand the other agent's messages and to answer them.

(i) the agents should learn the concepts that are most relevant for the tasks of the other agents; (ii) the agents should also learn concepts that are useful for communication, but not directly related to the tasks of the agents; (iii) the agents should not learn concepts that are irrelevant to their own tasks, even if these concepts are relevant for the tasks and for communication of the other agents.
(1) the optimal communication vocabulary is not unique and (2) the optimal communication vocabularies for the different agents are not identical.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the agents should use their common ground for learning new concepts in order to establish the best communication vocabulary.
the following questions: 1. How should agents communicate with each other when they have different ontologies?
the following questions: (i) Which concepts should be exchanged in order to enable the agents to understand the other agents' messages?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the optimal communication vocabulary is the union of all concepts that are relevant for the agents' tasks and the agents should learn the concepts of their partners that are relevant for their task.
the agents should learn the most general concepts of the different domains and that the communication vocabulary should consist of these concepts.
the optimal communication vocabulary depends on the specific application.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a model for the optimal alignment between heterogeneous ontologies in a multi agent system.
the agents should learn those concepts which are most important for the communication and which are least known to the agents.
we have developed a formalism that allows us to compute the optimal communication vocabulary for two agents with heterogeneous ontologies and to show that this vocabulary is unique.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in order to achieve optimal communication, it is not sufficient to learn the most informative concepts of the different agents, but it is crucial to learn the concepts that are most useful for the agents to communicate about.
the communication vocabulary should contain concepts from the ontologies that are used more often by the agents.
, under certain conditions, the optimal communication vocabulary is not necessarily the union of the concepts of all the individual ontologies.
